svg.aria-label: dmaguard — DMA / IOMMU attack-surface audit (demo fixture)

g.text: BOOT_IMAGE=/vmlinuz-6.8.0-45-generic root=/dev/nvme0n1p2 ro quiet splash iommu=pt
Thunderbolt domain0 security level 'none' without DMA protection
Any Thunderbolt device is connected automatically with PCIe tunnelling and no IOMMU
backstop — a plug-in DMA attack needs no user interaction.
Set the Thunderbolt security level to 'user' or 'secure' in firmware (and use
bolt/boltctl to authorise devices), or enable Kernel DMA Protection.
IOMMU in passthrough mode (14 identity-mapped group(s))
Identity domains give devices 1:1 access to physical memory — the IOMMU is present but
not isolating them. Thunderbolt/untrusted devices are still forced into DMA domains,
Drop iommu=pt / iommu.passthrough=1 unless required for performance; prefer
Firmware does not opt in to pre-boot DMA protection (DMAR)
DMA_CTRL_PLATFORM_OPT_IN is clear: firmware does not promise to keep VT-d protecting
memory across the boot-to-OS handoff. Windows Kernel DMA Protection and Linux
Thunderbolt `iommu_dma_protection` stay off on such platforms, and devices can DMA
Update firmware; enable 'Pre-boot DMA protection' / 'Kernel DMA Protection' /
'Thunderbolt DMA protection' in setup if offered.
Flush queues defer IOTLB invalidation, leaving a short window where a device can still
Boot with iommu.strict=1 on machines exposed to untrusted peripherals.
1 RMRR identity-mapped region(s) on non-legacy devices
Reserved Memory Region Reporting forces identity mappings that the IOMMU cannot fully
isolate. Expected for integrated graphics/USB; unusual elsewhere.
Devices behind external-facing ports; confirm each one is expected.
